claim: PTX ISA does not expose 5th-gen tensor-core integer MMA (tcgen05.mma .kind::i8) on sm_103a (B300), while it DID extend FP4 kinds to sm_103a
exact_field_or_evidence: Fetched full document 2026-08-11 and matched verbatim: 'Qualifier .kind::i8 is supported on following architectures: sm_100a sm_101a (Renamed to sm_110a from PTX ISA version 9.0) sm_110a' -- sm_103a ABSENT. Family-specific support carves it out: 'And is supported on following family-specific architectures from PTX ISA version 8.8 except .kind::i8 : sm_100f or higher in the same family ...' (the phrase 'except .kind::i8' occurs 4 times). Version-history table: 'tcgen05.mma Base variant 8.6 sm_100a 8.8 sm_100f 9.0 sm_110f | Kind .kind::i8 8.6 sm_100a 9.0 sm_110a'. CONTROL within the same instruction family: 'Kind .kind::mxf4nvf4 and .kind::mxf4 8.6 sm_100a 8.8 sm_103a 9.0 sm_110a'; 'K shape value 96 8.8 sm_103a'; 'tcgen05.shift Base variant 8.6 sm_100a 8.8 sm_103a 9.0 sm_110a'
caveat: STRONGEST finding so far and it is S1. NVIDIA extended mxf4/mxf4nvf4, tcgen05.shift and K-shape 96 to sm_103a in PTX 8.8 but never extended .kind::i8. So the software gap is not a framework choice - the 5th-gen integer MMA was never exposed at the ISA level on Blackwell Ultra, and the stack above had no option. Provides the MECHANISM for the 30x spec ratio: FP8 gets tcgen05, INT8 is left on legacy warp-level IMMA
